Postpartum Care

Postpartum care — involution, lochia, breastfeeding, postnatal danger signs and family planning guidance.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe postpartum changes in the mother
  • Assess involution and lochia
  • Support breastfeeding
  • Give postnatal danger sign advice

In simple words

The puerperium is the 6 weeks after delivery. During this period the uterus returns to its normal state (involution), lactation begins and the mother recovers.

Postpartum changes

Change Time
Uterus shrinks to non-pregnant size 6 weeks
Uterine fundus is felt at or below the umbilicus By day 2
Lochia changes from red to serous to white 3 weeks
Milk comes in after 3 days 3-5 days
Menstruation returns later 6-8 weeks, or later if breastfeeding

Assessing involution

  • Fundus by day 1 at the umbilicus, by day 2 one finger below; then descends about a finger daily
  • Firm, non-tender uterus that involutes is normal
  • Uterus that is tender, soft or high suggests retained products or infection
  • Lochia: rubra (red) for 3 days, serosa (brown/pink) for 7 days, alba (white) after 10 days, stopping by 3 weeks

Breastfeeding

  • Colostrum — first 2-3 days, rich in antibodies
  • Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months, complementary foods from 6 months
  • Correct attachment, frequent feeding, correct emptying of both breasts
  • Frequent feeding stimulates milk; assume feeding on demand
  • Watch for cracked nipples, engorgement and mastitis

Nutritional advice

Iron and folic acid, calcium, vitamin A; plenty of fluids; protein-rich and calorie-dense foods; green leafy vegetables; iodised salt; dietary care for anaemia

🔴 Postpartum haemorrhage is the leading cause of maternal death

Bleeding over 500 mL after birth, or a soft uterus with heavy lochia, is a medical emergency. Give oxytocin, massage the uterus, call for help and maintain intravenous access.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Puerperium lasts 6 weeks.
  2. The fundus descends about a finger daily and returns to the pelvis by 2 weeks.
  3. Lochia: rubra, serosa, alba.
  4. Colostrum gives immunity in the first days.
  5. Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months.
  6. Postpartum haemorrhage is the leading cause of maternal death.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Uterine tenderness and high position suggest infection or retained products.
  2. Mastitis presents with pain, fever and a red area; continue feeding.
  3. Postnatal exercises restore muscles and support.
  4. Contraception should start early after birth.
  5. Screen for postnatal depression.

📌 Memory trick

Lochia sequence: R-S-A — Rubra, Serosa, Alba.

60-second revision

  • Puerperium: 6 weeks of recovery.
  • Uterus involutes; fundus descends daily.
  • Lochia changes red, pink, white.
  • Colostrum first; exclusive breastfeeding 6 months.
  • Nutrition: iron, calcium, fluids, protein.
  • Danger: heavy bleeding, fever, foul discharge, severe headache, sadness.

Test yourself

The puerperium lasts:

Answer: B. The puerperium, the recovery period after childbirth, lasts 6 weeks.

Lochia alba appears at:

Answer: B. Lochia becomes white (alba) after about 10 days and stops by 3 weeks.

Colostrum is important because it:

Answer: B. Colostrum is rich in antibodies and proteins and protects the newborn from infection.

Exclusive breastfeeding should continue for:

Answer: B. Exclusive breastfeeding is advised for 6 months; complementary food starts at 6 months.

A soft uterus with heavy bleeding after delivery indicates:

Answer: B. A soft, lax uterus fails to clamp vessels and causes postpartum haemorrhage; give oxytocin and massage.
